correctness.rationale: Each of the 12 hyperflex and 16 ordinary lines is bitangent by exact substitution; all 28 lines are distinct in every odd characteristic, so the usual 28-odd-theta-characteristic count implies completeness. The finite list of 3276 triple determinants is checked by exact integer arithmetic in Z[t]/(t^4+1): 60 are identically zero, while all other 3216 norms have support only at 2,3,5,17. Thus outside three odd exceptional primes no new triple can become concurrent. For each exceptional odd prime, exhaustively computing the 378 pair intersections over a field containing an eighth root and all their incidences proves the complete (double,triple,quadruple) census. Frobenius permutes the explicit lines by exponent multiplication modulo eight and the exact incidence sets then supply all orbit cycles; independent pair counting checks 378 weighted incidences. The self-contained Python standard-library checker was actually executed and its output ends VERIFY_OK. The finite cases are exhaustive; the norm argument, not empirical interpolation, supplies the all-prime result.

value.rationale: The 28 bitangents are a canonical and historically studied configuration of the smooth Fermat plane quartic. Its 303 intersection points are a natural zero-dimensional geometric invariant. Determining the exact finite set of primes at which its incidence combinatorics degenerates is a motivated uniform specialization problem, not an arbitrary small-field example. The bad primes 3,5,17 include a qualitative collapse from 303 crossings to 63 fourfold points at p=3, with novel triple-concurrence strata at p=5 and p=17. The simultaneous q-Frobenius classification gives complete rational-point counts and zeta functions of each reduced crossing stratum over every finite extension; it is a useful arithmetic refinement, not merely a sample computation. These values are not implied by the previously published characteristic-zero 288/15 census without the independent determinant-norm and finite-field analysis.
